Sequential file processing and tests

Unit 1 · Week 7 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor, disposable quantities.txt copies and a test table. Main format: one non-negative integer on each line.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Sequential file processing and tests

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means read records sequentially, calculate a total and test stated assumptions. Learners distinguish empty, missing and malformed files. The first model assumes all records are suitable; later activities add an explicit rejection policy.

2. Retrieval: two checks on each record

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and paired correction

A line is text; strip removes whitespace; int converts suitable integer text; >=0 checks range. Invalid integer text raises ValueError. Ask learners to recall these steps individually then pair-check before processing multiple records.

3. A total from valid records

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher think-aloud and guided trace

Assume file exists and every line is a suitable non-negative integer. With lines 2,0,5, total moves 0,2,2,7 and output Total:7. Empty file body runs zero times, output 0. with handles closing. This model intentionally does not yet handle missing/malformed files, so state its assumptions before running.

4. A test table from the file contract

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent prediction and paired review

Expected one-record 5 total 5;2,0,5 total 7; empty total 0. Missing file raises FileNotFoundError. Under a reject-file policy, a negative or malformed record rejects whole file and no successful total is displayed. Learners distinguish expectations of the initial assumed-valid model from required behaviour of an improved version. Support: separate calculation and invalid-file tests.

5. A helper checks one record

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example and guided prediction

This helper returns an integer 0 or more for a suitable record, otherwise None. Predict parse_quantity(" 5\n")=5, "-3"=None, "three"=None and blank line=None. None is a distinct rejection signal because zero is valid. It does not itself read a file or decide how the caller reports failure. Strip/conversion/range combine Week 5 functions with Week 7 checks.

6. An explicit policy for unsuitable records

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent coding with optional scaffolds

Policy for this exercise: stop at first unsuitable record, report file rejected and do not display a partial total as successful. Reference structure: initialise total 0 and file_valid=True; read each line; call parse_quantity; if value is None set file_valid=False and break, else accumulate; after traversal display total only if file_valid. Handle FileNotFoundError separately with a missing-file message. Support: provide this scaffold. Test valid, empty, malformed, negative and missing cases. Stretch: track and report the rejected line number. Partners review evidence after independent work.

7. Empty and missing are different

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student hinge question

Correct B: an existing empty file opens and produces total 0 in the model; a missing file raises FileNotFoundError. FileNotFoundError differs from conversion ValueError. If several choose A, use two practice paths, one to an empty file and one absent. Do not replace a missing input with a new empty file silently.

8. Exit ticket: evidence for the policy

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

For lines 2,three,5, improved policy rejects on second line and displays no successful total; initial model would raise ValueError. Existing empty file total 0. Negative text converts but fails range. Ask learners to name a specific observed result for each policy test and retain it before controlled practical.
